A radiological imaging apparatus comprises a gantry that delimits an examination region intended to receive a part of a patient for analysis, and that follows a circular path of extension about a central axis. The gantry is provided with a radiation source arranged to emit radiation, a detector arranged to collect the radiation once it has crossed the examination region, and a casing that forms an internal housing space for both the source and the detector.

The casing is made up of a lower curved module and a further curved module that is movable relative to the lower curved module, thereby allowing the angular span of the casing to be changed. The gantry also includes a mechanism for moving the curved modules. This mechanism comprises a lower guide fixed to the lower curved module and defining a lower circular path of movement centered on the central axis, a movable guide fixed to the movable curved module and defining a circular movement path also centered on the central axis, and a thrust unit arranged to cooperate with the guides so as to drive rotation of the curved modules about the central axis.
outputs.L3:
The radiological imaging device includes a gantry defining an analysis area configured to receive and position at least a portion of a patient to be examined. The analysis area is arranged so that the relevant anatomical region can be placed in the correct position for acquiring radiological images.

The gantry houses a radiation source and a corresponding detector. During operation, the radiation source emits radiation toward the analysis area, and the detector is positioned to receive the radiation after it has passed through the patient or the portion of the patient located in the analysis area. In this way, the detector collects the information required to generate radiological images.

The radiation source and the detector are arranged within a casing of the gantry. This casing is formed by a bottom arched module and a movable arched module. The bottom arched module provides a supporting portion of the casing, while the movable arched module is configured to move relative to the bottom arched module. Together, the arched modules at least partially surround the analysis area and define the structural housing for the imaging components.

The movable arched module can be displaced with respect to the bottom arched module so as to vary the angular extension of the casing around the analysis area. This makes it possible to modify the configuration of the gantry, for example to facilitate access to the analysis area, adapt the device to different examination conditions, or adjust the relative positioning of the imaging components.

A movement apparatus is provided to control the movement of the arched modules. The movement apparatus includes circular guides and a thrust assembly. The circular guides define a curved path around a central axis of the gantry, while the thrust assembly applies the force required to move one or more of the arched modules along the guides. As a result, the arched modules can rotate around the central axis, allowing controlled adjustment of the casing’s angular extension and the positioning of the radiation source and detector relative to the analysis area.
outputs.L4:
A radiological imaging device comprises a gantry configured to support and position the main imaging components around an analysis area intended to receive at least part of a patient or object to be examined. The gantry includes a radiation source and a corresponding detector arranged so that radiation emitted by the source passes through the analysis area and is received by the detector for generating radiological image data. The source and detector may be mounted on or associated with a support structure that extends around a central axis of the gantry, the central axis generally corresponding to the longitudinal direction along which the patient or object is positioned.

The gantry further comprises a casing formed, at least in part, by one or more arched casing modules. These modules are arranged around the central axis and define the external profile of the gantry in the region surrounding the analysis area. Each arched casing module may extend over a predetermined angular portion of the gantry, so that, together, the modules at least partially surround the analysis area. The angular extension of the casing around the central axis is adjustable by moving one or more of the arched modules relative to the rest of the gantry.

To permit this adjustment, the imaging device includes a guide-and-thrust movement apparatus associated with the arched casing modules. The apparatus is configured both to guide the modules along a defined path and to apply the thrust necessary to move them in a controlled manner. In particular, the movement apparatus enables rotation of the arched casing modules about the central axis, allowing the angular coverage of the casing to be increased, reduced, or otherwise modified according to the operating requirements of the imaging procedure.

This configuration makes the gantry more adaptable to different clinical situations and patient positioning needs. By selectively rotating the arched casing modules, the device can provide improved access to the analysis area, facilitate patient loading and unloading, and allow the gantry casing to be configured according to the type of examination being performed. The adjustable casing also helps reduce obstruction around the patient while maintaining the structural and functional integration of the radiological imaging components.

Overall, the radiological imaging device provides a gantry structure in which the source, detector, and adjustable arched casing modules cooperate to define an imaging region around a central axis. The guide-and-thrust movement apparatus ensures reliable and controlled movement of the casing modules, thereby improving the flexibility, usability, and adaptability of the imaging gantry during radiological examinations.

**The Power of “The”**

“The” is one of the smallest words in the English language, yet it plays a very important role. It is called the definite article, and it helps us refer to a specific person, place, thing, or idea. For example, when we say “the book,” we are not talking about any book, but a particular book that the speaker and listener understand.

Although “the” is simple, it gives clarity and meaning to sentences. It can point to something already mentioned, such as “I saw a dog. The dog was friendly.” It can also refer to something unique, like “the sun,” “the moon,” or “the world.”

Because it appears so often, “the” may seem unimportant, but without it, English would feel incomplete and less precise. This small word helps connect ideas, guide understanding, and make communication smoother. In many ways, “the” proves that even the simplest words can have great importance.

counterfactuals.prompt: Draft a patent-style abstract for a radiological imaging device with a gantry having adjustable arched casing modules, a radiation source and detector, and a guide-and-thrust mechanism for rotating the modules around a central axis.
counterfactuals.output: A radiological imaging device comprises a gantry defining a central examination axis and including a plurality of arched casing modules arranged to at least partially surround an imaging volume. The arched casing modules are adjustable relative to one another to vary an access opening and/or an angular coverage of the gantry. A radiation source and a radiation detector are supported by one or more of the arched casing modules in mutually opposed or imaging-correlated positions. A guide-and-thrust mechanism is coupled to the arched casing modules and is configured to guide and drive rotation of the modules about the central axis, thereby selectively positioning the radiation source and detector around a subject disposed in the imaging volume. The mechanism may include guide tracks, rolling or sliding supports, and one or more actuators arranged to impart controlled circumferential movement while maintaining alignment of the modules. The adjustable modular gantry permits compact installation, improved patient access, and acquisition of radiological projection data over selected angular ranges.

counterfactuals.prompt: Write a single-paragraph technical description of a CT or radiological imaging gantry whose casing has a fixed bottom arched module and a movable arched module that changes the angular extension of the gantry.
counterfactuals.output: A radiological imaging gantry, such as for a CT scanner, comprises a generally annular support structure defining an examination aperture and enclosed by a segmented casing, wherein the casing includes a fixed bottom arched module extending around a lower circumferential portion of the gantry and rigidly coupled to a base or stationary frame, and a movable arched module arranged along an upper or lateral circumferential portion of the gantry and guided relative to the fixed bottom module between at least two operating positions. The movable arched module is configured to translate, rotate, slide, telescope, or otherwise shift along a curved path concentric or substantially concentric with the gantry opening, thereby selectively increasing or decreasing the angular extension of the casing around the aperture. In a closed or extended configuration, the movable arched module cooperates with the fixed bottom arched module to form a larger circumferential enclosure for imaging components, shielding, covers, cables, and service interfaces; in an open or retracted configuration, the movable arched module reduces the covered angular sector of the gantry to improve patient access, facilitate positioning, permit intervention near the imaging plane, or expose internal components for maintenance. The interface between the fixed and movable modules may include overlapping edges, seals, rails, hinges, locking elements, position sensors, and drive actuators to maintain alignment, structural rigidity, radiation shielding continuity, and safe operation during gantry adjustment.

counterfactuals.prompt: Describe in formal patent language a radiological scanner where the gantry defines an analysis area and includes arched modules movable along circular guides centered on the gantry axis.
counterfactuals.output:
A radiological scanner comprises a gantry defining an analysis area configured to receive at least a portion of a subject to be examined. The gantry has a gantry axis extending through the analysis area and includes a support structure provided with one or more circular guides arranged about, and centered on, the gantry axis.

The scanner further comprises a plurality of arched modules supported by the support structure. Each arched module extends along an arcuate path around at least a portion of the analysis area and is mounted to be movable along the circular guides about the gantry axis. The arched modules may be displaced circumferentially with respect to the gantry axis so as to vary their angular positions around the analysis area.

At least one of the arched modules carries one or more radiological components, such as an X-ray source, a radiation detector, a collimator, shielding element, or other imaging or irradiation component. Movement of the arched modules along the circular guides permits selective positioning of the radiological components relative to the subject and the analysis area, while maintaining the components on trajectories substantially concentric with the gantry axis.

In one embodiment, the circular guides are fixed to the gantry and define circular guide paths lying in planes substantially perpendicular to the gantry axis. The arched modules are slidably or rollingly coupled to the circular guides by respective guide-engaging members, thereby enabling controlled angular movement of each arched module around the gantry axis. The scanner may further comprise a drive system operatively coupled to the arched modules and configured to move the arched modules independently or in coordinated fashion along the circular guides.

The arrangement enables the scanner to modify the angular distribution of radiological components around the analysis area without requiring rotation of the entire gantry, thereby allowing flexible scanning geometries, improved access to the subject, and adaptable imaging configurations.

counterfactuals.prompt: Create a concise invention summary for a medical radiology device with a modular circular gantry, radiation source and detector housed in a casing, and movement apparatus using bottom/mobile guides and a thrust assembly.

The gantry is formed from separable modules to facilitate manufacture, transport, installation, and maintenance. A movement apparatus enables controlled positioning of the gantry, including bottom and/or mobile guide elements that constrain and direct gantry travel, together with a thrust assembly that applies driving force for translation or adjustment. The configuration provides stable, accurate movement of the imaging components while maintaining a compact, serviceable structure suitable for diagnostic or interventional radiology applications.
